history.period: 9th century AD - built by Chalukya king Baddega (Bhaddega), A.D. 850-895
history.summary: CSV TOWN CORRECTION: the CSV lists 'Karimnagar' as the town; the Bheemeshwara temple is at Vemulawada town (on the Mulavagu rivulet), now in Rajanna Sircilla district, ~35 km from Karimnagar city. Vemulawada was the capital of the Vemulawada Chalukyas (A.D. 750-973); the Bheemeshwara temple belongs to the 9th century AD and was built by Chalukya king Baddega (A.D. 850-895), hence historically called the Badhegeswara temple. It is about 1.5 km from the Vemulawada bus stand and walkable from the famous Sri Raja Rajeshwara Swamy temple. Dedicated to Shiva in Nagara style, it has had little renovation and retains historical authenticity; pujas are conducted per strict Vedic practice. Identity certainty: HIGH - the Vemulawada Bheemeshwara is the well-documented Chalukya shrine matching this name.

name: Bhimeswara Temple
town_description: Vemulawada is a temple town and mandal headquarters in Rajanna Sircilla district, Telangana, on the banks of the Mulavagu rivulet, ~35 km from Karimnagar city. Former capital of the Vemulawada Chalukyas (7th-10th century CE), nicknamed 'Dakshina Kashi'. Its main draw is the Sri Raja Rajeshwara Swamy temple; it also hosts the Bheemeshwara, Nagareshwara and Pochamma temples. Huge pilgrim crowds throng here during Maha Shivaratri and Sri Rama Navami.
